question: A current-carrying solenoid moves away from a fixed conducting loop. The direction of the induced current in the loop creates a magnetic pole on the face of the loop nearest to the solenoid. This pole will be:

options.A: The same as the nearest pole of the solenoid (Repulsion).
options.B: Opposite to the nearest pole of the solenoid (Attraction).
options.C: Always a North pole regardless of the solenoid's polarity.
options.D: Always a South pole regardless of the solenoid's polarity.
